cls: Antidiabetic / weight-management agent (dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist)
pharm: Dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist; stimulates glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppresses glucagon, delays gastric emptying, and reduces food intake
quick: 2.5 mg SC once weekly x4 weeks, then 5 mg weekly; may increase by 2.5 mg every >=4 weeks to 7.5, 10, 12.5, max 15 mg weekly
Any time of day, with or without food; same day each week
Not recommended; discontinue >=2 months before planned pregnancy (long half-life); weight loss not recommended in pregnancy
No human milk data; breastfeeding not recommended during treatment
No dose adjustment; monitor renal function if volume depletion from GI effects
No specific restriction; watch hypoglycemia with insulin/secretagogues
HbA1c, fasting glucose, body weight, renal function, MTC symptoms, pancreatitis and gallbladder symptoms
summary: Tirzepatide is a dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor co-agonist indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (Mounjaro), and for chronic weight management in adults with obesity or overweight with a weight-related comorbid condition (Zepbound). It lowers glucose in a glucose-dependent manner, suppresses appetite and delays gastric emptying, producing large HbA1c and body-weight reductions in the SURPASS and SURMOUNT trial programmes. It carries a boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors observed in rodents and is contraindicated with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2. The 2.5 mg dose is for initiation only and is not a maintenance dose.
indications: As an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (Mounjaro)

For chronic weight management in adults with obesity (BMI >= 30 kg/m2), or overweight (BMI >= 27 kg/m2) with at least one weight-related comorbid condition such as hypertension, dyslipidemia, type 2 diabetes, obstructive sleep apnea or cardiovascular disease (Zepbound), as an adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity

dosage.d: Start 2.5 mg once weekly for 4 weeks
dosage.t: Same day each week, any time, with or without food; abdomen, thigh or upper arm with site rotation
dosage.n: The 2.5 mg dose is for initiation only and is not effective as maintenance

dosage.d: After 4 weeks increase to 5 mg once weekly; if additional control needed after >=4 weeks, increase by 2.5 mg increments every >=4 weeks to 7.5 mg, 10 mg, 12.5 mg, maximum 15 mg once weekly
dosage.t: Reassess tolerance at each step; GI effects peak during escalation
dosage.n: Do not escalate faster than 2.5 mg every 4 weeks

dosage.d: Resume at the current maintenance dose if the break is short; retitrate from 2.5 mg if treatment is interrupted for a prolonged period or GI tolerance is lost

admin: Inject subcutaneously once weekly into the abdomen, thigh or upper arm; rotate sites within the same region
Give on the same day each week; the day may be changed if at least 72 hours separate two doses
May be given at any time of day, with or without food
Inspect solution; it should be clear and colorless to slightly yellow. Do not use if particulate matter or discoloration is present
Single-dose pens are for one-time use; discard after the dose is delivered
moa: Tirzepatide is a 39-amino-acid synthetic peptide that co-agonises both the GIP and GLP-1 receptors, with GIP-biased activity. Receptor activation increases glucose-dependent insulin secretion from pancreatic beta cells and suppresses glucagon secretion, lowering fasting and postprandial glucose with low intrinsic hypoglycaemia risk. Central GIP/GLP-1 signalling reduces appetite and food intake, and delayed gastric emptying (most marked after the first doses) contributes to satiety and weight loss.

absolute: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC)
Prior serious hypersensitivity reaction to tirzepatide or any excipient
relative: Concomitant insulin or insulin secretagogues (hypoglycaemia risk; reduce their dose)
Diabetic retinopathy (risk of temporary worsening with rapid glucose improvement)
Volume depletion risk with severe GI effects
monitor: Symptoms of medullary thyroid carcinoma (neck mass, dysphagia, dyspnoea, persistent hoarseness)
Renal function during significant GI adverse reactions

preg: Limited human data. Animal studies showed fetal growth and developmental effects at clinically relevant exposures. Because of the ~5-day half-life and 2-month washout, discontinue tirzepatide at least 2 months before a planned pregnancy. Weight loss offers no benefit during pregnancy and may cause fetal harm; use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk.
lact: There are no data on the presence of tirzepatide in human milk or its effects on the breastfed infant or milk production. Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment.
renal: No dosage adjustment is recommended in renal impairment, including end-stage renal disease. Monitor renal function when initiating or escalating therapy in patients with severe GI adverse reactions that could cause volume depletion and acute kidney injury.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is recommended in hepatic impairment; systemic exposure is similar across hepatic function. Use with usual GI-tolerance caution in severe impairment.

major: Insulin and insulin secretagogues such as sulfonylureas (increased risk of hypoglycaemia, including severe hypoglycaemia; reduce the concomitant dose)
moderate: Oral medications in general (delayed gastric emptying may alter the rate of absorption; monitor narrow-therapeutic-index drugs)
Combined oral contraceptives (tirzepatide delays absorption; switch to a non-oral contraceptive or add a barrier method for 4 weeks after initiation and after each dose escalation)
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; counsel on concomitant risks.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference; monitor disease-specific markers.

rare: Thyroid C-cell tumors / medullary thyroid carcinoma (rodent finding; human risk unknown)
Pulmonary aspiration during anaesthesia or deep sedation
emergency: Anaphylaxis or angioedema - stop drug and seek emergency care
Severe persistent abdominal pain radiating to the back (possible pancreatitis) - seek urgent evaluation
Severe hypoglycaemia with confusion or loss of consciousness

monitoring: HbA1c every 3 to 6 months and fasting glucose
Renal function, particularly during dose escalation or significant GI losses
Signs and symptoms of pancreatitis and gallbladder disease
Symptoms suggestive of thyroid tumors (neck mass, dysphagia, dyspnoea, persistent hoarseness)
Diabetic retinopathy status in at-risk patients
counsel: Take once weekly on the same day; you may change the day if at least 3 days separate doses
Nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea are most common while the dose is increasing and usually improve; stay hydrated and eat smaller, lower-fat meals
Report a neck lump, trouble swallowing, shortness of breath or persistent hoarseness (possible thyroid tumor symptoms)
Seek care for severe ongoing abdominal pain that may radiate to the back (possible pancreatitis)
If you use birth-control pills, use a barrier method or switch methods for 4 weeks after starting and after each dose increase
Tell anaesthesia and surgical teams you take tirzepatide before any procedure with sedation; discuss stopping at least 2 months before a planned pregnancy
pk: Glucose-lowering begins within days; appetite effects within 1-2 weeks
Plasma concentration peaks at 8 to 72 hours after a weekly dose
Present in circulation for about 4-5 weeks after the last dose; washout of ~2 months before planned pregnancy
Refrigerate at 2-8 C; may be kept at room temperature up to 30 C for a maximum of 21 days; do not freeze; protect from light
pearls: Dual GIP/GLP-1 agonism produced superior HbA1c and weight reductions vs selective GLP-1 agonists in SURPASS (diabetes) and SURMOUNT (weight) trials
The 2.5 mg dose is for initiation only and is not a maintenance dose
Delayed gastric emptying is most marked early and transiently impacts oral drug absorption (notably oral contraceptives)
GI tolerability is managed by slow escalation, smaller low-fat meals and hydration rather than stopping outright
missed: If a dose is missed, give it as soon as possible within 4 days (96 hours); if more than 4 days have passed, skip it and resume the regular weekly schedule. Do not take two doses within 3 days of each other.
overdose: Overdose may produce severe nausea, vomiting and hypoglycaemia (especially with insulin or secretagogues). There is no specific antidote. Initiate supportive treatment guided by signs and symptoms with extended observation given the ~5-day half-life. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
